name: L293D Motor Driver
summary: Quad half-bridge with built-in flyback diodes: two DC motors bidirectionally, or one bipolar stepper. Old, inefficient and still the part in every starter kit.
notes: It is a Darlington bridge, so it drops roughly 1.4-1.8 V on each side, about 3 V total. At 6 V in, your motor sees half that. This is the reason to reach for a DRV8833 or TB6612FNG instead.
600 mA continuous per channel, 1.2 A peak. The plain L293 doubles that but has no internal diodes.
The four center pins (4, 5, 12, 13) are both ground and the only heatsink. Solder all four to a copper pour; a DIP socket in still air will thermally shut down.
VCC1 (16) is logic and VCC2 (8) is the motor rail. Both are required, and VCC2 must be at or above VCC1.
The two enable pins take PWM for speed control. PWM on the direction inputs instead works but is noisier and gives a worse low-speed response.
The D in L293D means the clamp diodes are on-die. With a bare L293 you must add eight external Schottkys.

pins.name: EN1,2
pins.note: High to drive. PWM here for speed control on motor A.

pins.name: GND
pins.note: One of four fused ground pins, the package's entire thermal path.

pins.name: VCC2
pins.note: Needs a bulk electrolytic close by; motor current comes from here, not from your 5 V rail.

pins.name: EN3,4
pins.note: PWM here for speed control on motor B.

pins.name: VCC1
pins.note: Separate from the motor rail. 100 nF at the pin.

circuit.title: Driving one motor

parts.why: Logic supply, 4.5 to 7 V. Separate from the motor rail and it must be powered first.
Motor supply, up to 36 V. Tying it to the logic rail only works if the motor runs on 5 V.
Decoupling on the logic supply at the pin.
Bulk on the motor supply. Stall current comes from here, not from the logic rail.
A brushed motor across one half bridge. IN1 and IN2 set direction, EN1,2 gates both outputs.
Enable tied high runs the bridge continuously. Drive it with PWM instead to control speed.

circuit.note: The D suffix is the whole difference: the L293D has the clamp diodes on-die, the plain L293 does not and needs eight external ones. Both drop about 2 V across the output stage, so a 12 V motor on a 12 V rail sees closer to 10 V.
